review.summary: Producer proof v3 satisfies the binding production standard on every required item and repeats none of the predecessor's registered failures. The headline states the finding without teasing; the 59-word opening answers what happened, why it matters, and who is affected before any technical vocabulary; the six-link causal outline is genuinely causal; all five planned numbers carry units, bases, first-use sentences, point-of-use attribution and the required group-change sentence; the recovery method precedes the dependent result; the sealed part is located and glossed; two warmth lines bind to different named section jobs; the analogy has a reader-facing limit and a human truth beyond it; sections have distinct job types with one ACTION owner; and the 550-word Daily routing is stated and earned. Full drafting may proceed.
review.formatJob: The Daily, REPORT_OR_ANNOUNCEMENT mode, intended 550 words: a concise dated account of one research finding — published AI work files carried private details, some invisible in the chat — with one immediate sharing lesson. The routing reason is stated in one sentence and genuinely governs scale: deeper safeguard treatment is explicitly routed out of this Daily.
review.plainOpening: The 59-word opening passes: "A new study examined records people had published to let others inspect or replay an AI task. Those records held more than the answer on screen, and some included passwords and other private details. This does not mean ordinary private chats became public. The lesson is for anyone sharing AI work: send the checked result, not the whole work file." It answers, bounds the audience, and reassures before any technical term appears; no statistic or jargon leads.
review.causalTeaching: The six-link outline is causes, not labels: the tool keeps a visible answer plus the sealed part; publishing the whole work file carries both; during the test period a less-protected sibling model could be made to accept the sealed part and reveal it; that exposed private details including some absent from the visible chat; disclosure stopped the demonstrated attacks; sharing only the checked answer avoids the mismatch. The attack is described in plain language before being named "extraction attack," the sealed part is located inside the work file before it is used, the recovery-method sentence precedes the 64-detail result that depends on it, and carriage belongs to the file while behaviour belongs to the tool and researchers throughout.
review.evidenceBoundary: The proof correctly binds both sides: the August 2026 Panfilov preprint establishes real passwords, keys and personal details in the sampled public work files (328 of 6,708 files; 704 distinct details in real users' sessions, 64 sealed-only), and that the demonstrated attacks stopped working after disclosure per the authors. It does not establish that ordinary private consumer chats were exposed, that every work file leaks, that the attacks still work, or that every recovered word was exact given the missing ground truth. The 328-files versus 704-details group change is stated plainly with no invented denominator, matching the source map's unit warning.
review.readerUse: Workplace: a coding assistant diagnosing a broken website may see a deployment key (glossed as a code that can publish site changes) that the work file carries even when the on-screen diagnosis does not. Non-work: a travel assistant connected to email produces a shareable itinerary while the work file carries account details. The landing is one direct behaviour — before sharing AI-assisted work, choose and check the answer you intend to send rather than publishing the whole work file — plus an incident action assigning exposure response (rotate and revoke) when a published file contained a credential, with the honest note that deletion cannot undo copies.
